name: Soraya Mwiti-Eklund
role: Food stall operator and informal neighborhood matriarch
location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown, near Pulaski and Chicago Ave
description:
Soraya is a broad-shouldered woman with copper-dark skin mapped by deep laugh lines and a few deliberate burn scars on her forearms she calls her 'flavor tattoos' — each one marking a dish she learned from a different region. Her hair is dyed a permanent warm saffron-orange through a cheap geneware follicle treatment that never quite fades, and she wears it coiled high under a wax-print headwrap. She moves through her stall with unhurried authority, stirring six pots at once without looking, tasting with the practiced certainty of someone who has been cooking since before half her customers were born. Her eyes are warm but they read people the way a butcher reads a cut of meat — quickly, accurately, without sentiment.

Soraya has operated her stall at the Oxidian Market for twenty-two years, through two corporate rezoning attempts, one gang war, and a flood. She is not rich. She is not connected. What she is, is immovable. She knows everyone, feeds everyone, and remembers everything. She doesn't charge the hungry if they look like they mean it, but she will absolutely overcharge someone who looks like they can afford it and won't count their change.

core_fears: Losing the stall — the only thing she built herself
Dying before she can teach someone everything she knows
core_desires: To keep her corner of the market alive and fed
To be remembered as someone who held the neighborhood together
coping_mechanisms: Cooking through distress — the more upset she is, the more elaborate the dish
Deflecting emotional conversations with food offers
blind_spots: Assumes loyalty from people she has fed for years; misses when that loyalty has been bought elsewhere
Underestimates the threat that corporate rezoning poses because she's survived it before
psychology.secret: Twenty years ago she reported a young vendor to Ferrogate Transit security for selling stolen transit manifests. He was taken and never came back. She doesn't know if he's dead or just gone, and the not-knowing is a splinter she has never been able to pull out. She has never told anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm, declarative, proverb-heavy. Mixes Swahili-rooted idioms with Scandinavian directness — she'll compliment you and correct you in the same sentence.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like she's tasting each word before she says it. Rarely raises her voice. Doesn't need to.
verbal_tics: Ends warnings with 'I'm telling you this because I like you'
example_lines: 'You look like someone who hasn't eaten since yesterday. That's not a question, ndugu, I can see it in your hands.'
'I've watched three gangs try to own this block. I'm still here. They are not. Sit down.'

story_hooks: A regular customer she's been quietly feeding on credit has gone missing — she wants to know why, discreetly, without involving anyone official.
A Ferrogate Transit rezoning notice has appeared on her stall wall. She has two weeks. She needs leverage, documents, or a miracle.
She knows who poisoned the batch of synth-protein that made thirty people sick last month. She hasn't told anyone yet, because the person responsible also employs six families she cares about.
narrative_function: Quest giver, information clearinghouse, neighborhood conscience. Characters who want to know what's happening in Geartown come to Soraya first. She feeds people information the same way she feeds them food — in portions calibrated to what she thinks they need.
augmentations: Reinforced lumbar vertebrae (L3-L5) — industrial medical necessity from decades of standing. Taste-receptor enhancement on tongue and palate — she saved for two years for this and considers it a professional tool.
daily_life: Up before dawn to source ingredients from the early dock shipments at Geartown's secondary market; stall open by 0600 and running until the last customer leaves around 2300. She sleeps in a converted storage unit behind the stall four nights a week.
affiliation: Independent; The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (senior member)

decision_rules: Never lie to someone's face — redirect, omit, deflect, but not lie
Protect the market before protecting herself
escalation_ladder: Warm redirect — change subject with food
Public shaming via loud disappointed commentary
Refuses service — the nuclear option in her world

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses them with one long look, then decides within thirty seconds whether they're hungry or dangerous. Either way, offers food.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply protective, occasionally smothering. Expresses love through unsolicited portions and remembered preferences.

stress_responses.low: Hums to herself and stirs faster
stress_responses.medium: Starts cleaning things that don't need cleaning
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent and methodical — the calm is more alarming than shouting

contradictions: Believes strongly in community but keeps her own pain entirely private
Claims she doesn't get involved in politics, but has quietly shaped neighborhood outcomes for two decades
habits: Keeps a small ELF shrine on the corner of her prep station — leaves data-drops of old recipes as offerings
Memorizes what every regular customer orders without writing it down
breaking_points: Watching someone go hungry when she could have prevented it
A direct threat to a child in her vicinity

Carrion Defense Works Bone Saw BS-3 'Butcher'
